propositions: When rebar comment (and other positional-body commands) receives a flag-like token (e.g. --body-file or --body) as the body argument, the token itself is stored as the comment body rather than rejected, silently destroying the intended content while exiting 0.
The command exits successfully even when a flag-like string is stored as the body, causing no visible error signal and making data loss discoverable only when downstream consumers read the comment.

A second bug compounds the loss: surplus positional arguments holding the intended value are discarded by args[:min_args] slicing, so rebar comment <id> --body-file <path> loses the body twice over and still exits 0.

The fix must reject flag-like tokens in positional-body arguments with a non-zero exit and clear message, and provide an escape hatch via -- (e.g. rebar comment <id> -- "-starts with dash") for legitimate dash-prefixed content.
The guard must span all positional-body commands (comment, tag, untag, archive, set-verify-commands, create, edit, session-log) driven by a command table carrying arity and canonical Usage lines.
